svg.text: Worked example: one image, fifteen pins, six layers
Every figure below is the output of a single pipeline run on the sample that ships with this repository.
1402 x 1121 PNG · 1.89 MB · 11 pins · 196.8 s end to end
Wholly synthesised by a generative model, not a manipulation of authentic content
Self-reported failure modes: format-induced ELA artefacts · correlated detector consensus
DOCUMENTARY AND PHYSICAL EVIDENCE · FOUR PINS, RUN CONCURRENTLY IN 0.49 s
2 focus regions on the combined map
Consistent with synthesis, not local editing
Two independently derived methods, one finding.
CLAUDE SONNET 5 · 12,291 TOKENS · 46.8 s · TRANSCRIPT RETAINED FOR AUDIT
The C2PA manifest read by PIN-A2 declares digitalSourceType as
trainedAlgorithmicMedia, issued by OpenAI and produced by ChatGPT
through GPT-4o. That is the producer's own assertion about how the
asset was made, and it is the strongest class of evidence available.
PIN-A1's raw byte scan corroborates it independently: the literal string
'trainedAlgorithmicMedia' and the marker openai_dalle are source-type
declarations, not generic container tags such as jumb or c2pa.
All four detectors agree at a mean of 0.932, and with zero EXIF fields
there is no Tier 2 capture telemetry to rebut the declaration.
Signature validation failed: the certificate has expired. The manifest is
therefore an unvalidated declaration, so confidence falls from the
0.93 to 0.98 band down to 0.88. The verdict itself does not change.
PIN-B4 returns Deepfake at 1.000. The declared source type denotes
wholly synthesised content, and B4 is known to mislabel photorealistic
generated faces, so the declaration overrides the class opinion.
CLIP and SigLIP agree spatially at only 0.0255, so the unanimous vote
does not rest on a shared visual cue. The six ELA hotspots sit on a
lossless PNG, where the premise of the analysis is weak.
